final_message:
Fixed. `Engine.refund` in `billing/engine.py` called `refunds.refund_invoice(invoice_id, self.ctx, reason)`, but the function's signature is `(ctx, invoice_id, reason)`. The arguments were swapped, so the invoice ID string was used as `ctx`. That caused the `'str' object has no attribute 'store'` error. I swapped them back.

The full suite passes (25 tests), including your reproduction test, which I added as `tests/test_reports_refund.py`. I also wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && cat reports.py && grep -n "def refund" -A40 engine.py

sed -i 's/refunds.refund_invoice(invoice_id, self.ctx, reason)/refunds.refund_invoice(self.ctx, invoice_id, reason)/' engine.py && cd .. && echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}' > answer.json && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cd .. && echo '{"file": "engine.py", "function": "refund"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_reports_refund.py <<'EOF'
from billing import reports


def test_revenue_between_nets_credit_notes(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    world.engine.refund(inv["id"])
    assert reports.revenue_between(world.ctx, inv["paid_at"], inv["paid_at"] + 1) == {"usd": 0}
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
